newsitem.title: GERMANY: Analysts welcome news Lufthansa may sell Cargolux.
newsitem.headline: Analysts welcome news Lufthansa may sell Cargolux.

text.p: Analysts welcomed news on Tuesday that Deutsche Lufthansa Cargo, a unit of German airline Lufthansa AG, was in talks with Swissair to sell its 24.5 percent stake in Cargolux of Luxembourg.

"It's not a majorly important item for Lufthansa, but the airline has been losing money in the cargo area, even though it says will break-even this year. Some disposals in this area are not a bad idea in any case," a Frankfurt-based share analyst said.
Luxembourg airline Luxair owns 30.5 percent of Cargolux, while the remainder is held by numerous Luxembourg financial institutions and holding companies.

Lufthansa Cargo said earlier that talks were going on but would not comment on the status of the talks. It said a decision on any sale of the stake to Swissair was expected in the second half of September.
Swissair-Schweizerische Luftverkehr AG later confirmed that negotiations were under way, but would not elaborate much further.

"We are looking at how the two companies could cooperate optimally. What exactly will arise from this is the point of the talks," the Swissair spokesman said, saying it was still open whether this could lead to a takeover or taking a financial stake.
Lufthansa has said that it sees a chance of a profit in 1997 in its trouble cargo division, after the business reported an operating profit in the first four months of the year.

Lufthansa's cargo unit has been hurt by falling prices in the air freight market. The business reported a loss on ordinary activities of 59.8 million marks in 1996 despite a three percent rise in sales to 3.43 billion marks.
In the first quarter, the cargo unit reported an 11 percent rise in sales to 872 million marks.
Cargolux saw net profit of $7.33 million in 1996, down from $15.31 million in 1995. Freight carried in 1996 rose to a new record of 233,914 tonnes from 217,057 tonnes.
Revenues rose to $396.66 million from $389.07 million.
Cargolux operates a fleet of three Boeing 747-400Fs and is to take delivery of a further two 400Fs in August and November this year. It also operates four Boeing 747-200s, including one on leaseback.
